messages:
maya: Quick follow-up to the canary RFC — I'm proposing a refactor I sketched called the 'swing gatekeeper' to separate decisioning from actuators and enable a low-latency local fallback path. Thoughts?

devin: short tl;dr? curious how this differs from the current fallback-orch.

maya: Current flow: central policy -> router instructs runtime to shift traffic. Problem: control plane latency and per-request stalls during outage of central services.

maya: Proposal: keep central policy for long-lived decisions but introduce a lightweight local gatekeeper in the runtime that can make emergency fallback decisions based on compact signals (probe health, local queue depth, recent error rate). Local gatekeeper has a tiny, auditable DSL and a single-source of truth hash from control plane for policy updates.

olga: So local decisions only for emergencies? How do we avoid split-brain where local decides to fallback but central is still rolling traffic forward?

maya: Yes, emergency-only. Rules: local can only reduce traffic to older variant or degrade features (e.g., disable prefix caching or batching). It cannot permanently flip canary percentages. It also emits an urgent event to central with causal digest.

samir: What signals exactly? cpu/gpu load, p95 latency, kv cache miss spike, error-rate? Need to keep it very small.

maya: Minimal set: local p95 > threshold, error-rate > x, request queue length > y, probe failures > z in window. Anything else we can stream to central for richer adjudication, not for local gating.

rachel: Concern: observability. If locals trigger fallback, we need end-to-end trace to debug who triggered it and why. Also runbook for oncall.

maya: Agreed. Design enforces a fallback-event envelope that includes: local policy hash, signal snapshot (compact), and last-central-decision-timestamp. That gets emitted and replicated to central audit log.

tony: How do we handle tenant-scoped policies vs cluster defaults? We already do per-tenant latency budgets.

maya: Local gatekeeper evaluates in order: tenant-specific overrides -> compute-safe defaults. Central publishes a per-tenant compact policy blob; runtime caches it with TTL. If blob missing/expired, local only applies cluster defaults.

devin: Any config example?

maya: Here's a tiny policy snippet (pseudo-DSL):

```
policy "local-fallback-v1" {
  scope: tenant
  emergency_rules: [
    {signal: p95_ms, op: ">", value: 1200, action: fallback_variant("stable")},
    {signal: error_rate, op: ">=", value: 0.03, action: throttle(0.3)},
    {signal: queue_len, op: ">", value: 50, action: shed(gradual)}
  ]
  audit_level: verbose
}
```

olga: Nice. A couple of open questions: 1) How does this play with session affinity? 2) What about KV cache and stateful sessions? If we fallback to stable we might lose warm KV entries.

maya: For affinity: local gatekeeper prefers same-variant only if session-boundary not violated. For stateful caches we add a hint header so the router can steer to instances with warm cache when possible; but emergency fallback may accept cache coldness as tradeoff.

samir: What about rollout metrics — we need to avoid local fallback masking central metrics and hiding regressions.

maya: Plan: when local triggers, central marks canary as 'degraded-by-local' and we annotate metrics and slow down automatic progression. Also have a 'replay window' where we rerun a sample of canary traffic through central telemetry to validate.

rachel: Runbook notes: oncall sees an alert with event_id and can jump to UI to replay sample and optionally force central override. Also: allow a one-click 'suppress local fallback' for emergency mitigation.

tony: Security: local policy blobs must be signed by control plane to prevent rogue pods flipping rules.

maya: yep - HMAC of blob, versioned and stored in attestation log.

devin: ops cost: more code paths in runtime. Can we keep the gatekeeper as a tiny shim (C++ or Rust) that only depends on a minimal set of metrics to remain auditable and easy to fuzz-test?

maya: That's the plan. Minimal dependencies, deterministic eval, property tests.

samir: Backoff/TTL semantics — if local falls back, when does it re-evaluate to rejoin the canary? Immediate probing vs exponential backoff?

maya: Exponential backoff with probe ramp: after fallback, local will run a probe stream (configurable low qps) to canary variant. If X consecutive probes pass within window, resume partial traffic at a reduced rate and notify central.

olga: Could we reuse the existing probe/oracle infra and just add a gated fast-path for verdicts? Would be less churn.

maya: Good point — propose to plug into probe-oracle. Local gatekeeper subscribes to condensed probe results instead of raw metrics where possible.

devin: Any UI impacts? Need obvious flags in Console for which tenants have local emergency allowed.

rachel: And alerting — separate alert channel + scoreboard metric for 'local fallbacks per hour' to spot flapping.

maya: I'll draft a short RFC with diagrams: control-plane -> publish signed blob -> runtime cache -> local gatekeeper -> emergency action -> audit event -> central adjudication. Will include probe reuse, TTLs, HMAC, and runbook steps.

deploy-bot: Deployment note:         New gatekeeper component will be rolled as opt-in feature flag on dedicated clusters for initial canary.

devin: Love it. Can you add a variant teardown spec? e.g., when fallback persists for > N minutes, automated rollback if central also sees degradation.

maya: Yes, auto-rollback criteria will be part of central policy; local will only signal. I'll include thresholds.

olga: Sounds promising. +1 to a focused RFC. Thanks Maya.

maya: Thanks all — I'll post the RFC link when it's ready. :rocket:
